  "rationale": "Resubmission of the round-1 accepted program (objective [4,28,2]); it is provably lexicographically optimal. Wait bound: all four expected origins are distinct, so each slot (one page, value from a single read) serves exactly one destination; 4 slot-uses / 2 slots force >=2 rounds. In each round, publish requires an initialized value with no pending read, and the only way to observe read completion is blocking wait_reads, so each round needs >=1 wait_reads. Reusing a slot requires release, which requires no pending transfer on the slot; since a non-wait op invalid at ANY reachable state is unsafe, wait_writes must precede every release round, giving >=1 wait_writes per round. Hence >=4 waits; 1-slot scheduling would need 8, and interleaving rounds cannot share waits because round-2 reads cannot be issued until slots are freed by wait_writes+release, which is after round-1's wait_reads. Command bound: each slot-use strictly needs reserve/read/publish/acquire/write/release (write needs acquired+initialized; acquire needs published; final state needs all slots free), i.e. 24 + 4 waits = 28; no op is droppable and no write can serve two distinct destinations. Peak live slots is 2, the task's slot count, already minimal given two concurrent reads are needed to keep one round. Trace-safety: reads target distinct slots, writes target distinct destinations, and every non-wait op is enabled under all DMA completion orders (verified by the native filter's 51-state exploration)."
